name: Zambia

findings.local_actor: Ministry of Home Affairs (Lusaka CCTV / Safe City, Public Security Network Project phase III)
findings.summary: ZTE is general contractor for Zambia's US$210m Lusaka CCTV 'safe city' system, financed by a US$178.5m China Development Bank loan; government said in August 2022 it was 98% complete and would proceed.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 4 not 5: construction started December 2017 and reported 98% complete, but full operation not confirmed (AidData found no completion evidence as of Feb 2022). Equipment rule: ZTE as vendor sets pole prc. AidData also records a separate US$78.6m Citi UK loan (2017). Announced value is the 2013 contract figure; the minister called the cost too high and promised a review.

findings.reversal_of: January 2013 US$210m Ministry of Home Affairs - ZTE CCTV contract
findings.summary: Zambia's government cancelled the original single-sourced US$210m ZTE CCTV contract for Lusaka in September 2013 over corruption allegations; the project was later re-tendered and returned to ZTE with CDB financing.
findings.analyst_inference: Reversal coded regulatory (procurement integrity), so it does not move the map; it was effectively undone when ZTE resumed as contractor (ZMB-001). Tier 3 because a signed contract was reversed.

findings.controller: Government of Zambia (ZICTA / Smart Zambia; Zambia National Data Centre)
findings.financier: Chinese government concessional loans (Chinese state-owned banks)
findings.summary: Huawei built Zambia's Tier III national data centre in Lusaka under the US$75m Smart Zambia phase 1, financed by Chinese concessional loans; it opened at ZICTA in early 2017 to host government and commercial data.
findings.analyst_inference: Owner-operator rule gives domestic; Huawei is builder, Chinese state lenders financier. But the WSJ (via Lusaka Times) reported in 2019, from anonymous officials, that about half the ~40 staff at the ZICTA data centre were Huawei employees who helped trace opposition bloggers' phones; Huawei denied it. If confirmed, Huawei operating access would make the controller prc. IT equipment vendor inside not stated explicitly. Current status not checked; pre-2020.

findings.reversal_of: Smart Zambia phase II (Huawei-implemented, China EXIM-financed e-government programme)
findings.summary: Zambia stopped Smart Zambia phase II, a US$333.2m e-government project to be implemented by Huawei with China EXIM Bank funding, in August 2022, cancelling undisbursed Chinese loans to contain debt.
findings.analyst_inference: Layer coded facilities because phase II reportedly included further national data centres (per 2017 ITWeb); exact scope mix (e-services, network, facilities) not confirmed, and pole prc reflects Huawei as implementer of the cancelled package. Reversal coded commercial (debt management), so it does not move the map. Not corroborated: The EastAfrican confirms ~US$1.6bn of undisbursed China EXIM/ICBC loans cancelled incl. ICT projects but does not name Smart Zambia. Tier 3 assumes a contracted package; loan signature not verified. ITWeb says some components will be finished from the budget.

findings.summary: MTN Zambia launched Zambia's first commercial 5G network in November 2022 with Huawei, after an 11-month trial, covering parts of Lusaka, Kitwe, Ndola, Chingola, Solwezi and Kalumbila.
findings.analyst_inference: Equipment rule: Huawei as 5G vendor gives prc. Whether Huawei is sole RAN/core vendor for MTN Zambia is not stated. Further reports seen only in search results were on PRC state-media hosts and were not fetched or cited. Corroboration fails because the second source was not opened.

findings.summary: Zambia's communications minister said in 2019 Huawei was contracted to upgrade state-owned Zamtel's radio network and government towers to 5G-capable equipment; Huawei was already building Zamtel towers. Huawei donated 25 more towers, passed to Zamtel, in August 2024.
findings.analyst_inference: Two opened S2 sources, but they evidence different events (2019 upgrade contract claim; 2024 tower donation), so not counted as corroboration of the tier-3 contract. No contract value, timescale or award notice found. Towers are passive infrastructure; the 2024 donation shows continuing Huawei-Zamtel ties rather than a new active-equipment award.

findings.summary: Ericsson won a contract in March 2016 to modernise Airtel Zambia's radio access network nationwide, transforming its 2G and swapping out its 3G sites, with software and services.
findings.analyst_inference: Ericsson is Swedish, so pole third. Pre-2020 and still_current not checked; Airtel Zambia's current 4G/5G RAN and core vendors not identified in this pass. Value undisclosed. Medium on the single opened S1 company release.

findings.summary: Paratus Zambia opened a carrier-neutral 1 MW data centre in Lusaka in July 2021, with redundant connectivity, power and cooling.
findings.analyst_inference: Paratus is a Namibia-headquartered group, so owner-operator pole third (analyst knowledge of headquarters, not stated in the opened source). Small facility; investment value not stated.

findings.summary: Liquid Intelligent Technologies signed an MOU with Zambia's government on 7 March 2023 at the LDC5 conference in Doha to build a data centre for local businesses and hyperscalers; no value, capacity or timeline given.
findings.analyst_inference: Liquid is part of Cassava Technologies (pan-African group founded by Zimbabwean Strive Masiyiwa), so pole third; home jurisdiction not stated in source. Year of signing inferred from the article URL date and the LDC5 conference timing. Construction status unknown.

findings.summary: SMART Zambia and Huawei signed an MOU at the May 2026 Zambia Mobile Congress to jointly support a National AI Data Centre, plus training 5,000 ICT professionals through Huawei programmes by 2028; no value or site disclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: owner-operator not stated. If SMART Zambia owns and operates it, the facility pole is domestic; Huawei's role (equipment vendor, builder, operator) is unspecified, and Huawei-supplied IT or accelerators would be a prc silicon/equipment finding. Follows the Huawei-built 2017 national data centre (ZMB-003).

findings.local_actor: Ministry of Technology and Science; University of Zambia (ZAMREN)
findings.summary: Google and Zambia's government signed an MoU in mid-2024 to set up an AI Centre of Excellence at the University of Zambia, hosted by the ZAMREN research network, for young innovators; no funding figure disclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Layer models is approximate: a capacity hub, not adoption of a Google model by government. Tier 1 (MoU). Whether the centre has opened was not checked.

silicon.null_reason: no accelerator purchases, GPU deployments or export-licence reporting for Zambia surfaced in data-centre and AI searches

power.null_reason: no AI/data-centre-specific power evidence surfaced; budget spent on other layers

research_gaps: Is the ZTE Lusaka CCTV/safe city system now fully operational, and did the 2022 Home Affairs cost review change it?
Did Huawei staff operate or hold access to the ZICTA national data centre (WSJ 2019 allegation), and who operates it today?
Exact scope and contract status of Smart Zambia phase II before its 2022 cancellation, and which components were completed from the budget.
Current RAN/core vendors for MTN, Airtel and Zamtel 4G/5G; whether Huawei is sole 5G vendor at MTN Zambia.
Owner, site, value and equipment vendor of the planned National AI Data Centre under the 2026 SMART Zambia-Huawei MOU.
Status of Liquid's Zambia data centre and the Google AI Centre of Excellence at UNZA.
Any national AI model, government LLM adoption, or accelerator purchases in Zambia.
